correctness.rationale: The projector decomposition H=A^{1/2}ΠA^{1/2} yields exactly two positive Nyström eigenvalues λ and 1, λ∈[1,k]. The nontrivial generalized pencil yields exact trace T and determinant D, with its extreme eigenvalues straddling the untouched eigenvalue 1+m. The condition-number sign equals minus the sign of G(λ), whose t=(λ−1)/(k−λ) transform is a cubic with strictly positive cubic/quadratic coefficients and strictly negative linear/constant coefficients, yielding exactly one root. Exact rational substitution verifies the explicit worsening witness; Gaussian full support and continuity prove positive probability. Dimension-two cases and the 32/27 limit are separately proved. SymPy verifies identities and a direct-scatter numerical experiment checks 500 sketches (2008 assertions) without treating finite evidence as universal proof.

originality.rationale: The initiating paper defines and analyzes the same normalized Nyström preconditioner, but its large-sketch expected-condition-number bound is not a deterministic per-sketch comparison. This result obtains a complete and sharp three-dimensional one-parameter condition-number sign classification, including both positive-measure worsening and improving sketches for every spike and regularization, explicit exact witness and minimal dimension. A targeted comparison with spectral limited-memory and multilevel sketched preconditioning found differing operators/claims rather than an implication of the exact cubic threshold. The priority risk of an unobserved equivalent elementary-pencil calculation remains.
residual_risks: An unobserved equivalent rank-two spectral-pencil computation in numerical preconditioning literature cannot be ruled out by searches.
The multilevel preconditioning paper was compared at abstract level only; no full-text NOT_COVERING assertion is made.
The model is diagonal with a repeated eigenvalue, rank-two and exact arithmetic; broad numerical conclusions outside the stated domain are not asserted.

value.rationale: An SPD preconditioner can be computationally worthwhile yet worsen conditioning for a particular sketch; determining whether its intended improvement is guaranteed is a natural structural safety question. This theorem establishes a complete sharp sketch-angle classification for the smallest possible dimension, all spike strengths and all positive regularizations; the deterioration and improvement each have positive Gaussian probability, with an exact rational witness and a nontrivial asymptotic 32/27 amplification family. The threshold is more informative than a bare single counterexample. It does not purport to establish iteration-count worsening or universal higher-dimensional bounds.
